1→# PROJECT: Ryde — Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution
   2→
   3→**Status: BUILT, IN POLISH (updated 2026-10-07).** The system runs end to end on the mock and on
   4→the real Tencent model; the application build freezes on **12 Oct 2026** (operator ruling), after
   5→which only recording, documentation and deploy work continue. Building started 2026-09-21. Planning closed **2026-09-19** and the scope, stack and
   6→workflow are ruled. This file is CodeBuddy's memory for this project: the builder's entry
   7→point. The ruled scope lives in
   8→the planning repository and is deliberately unreadable from here (the permission fence in
   9→`.codebuddy/settings.json` denies reads of that path, and it is verified to work), so
  10→**everything you need is in this file, `docs/` and the kickoff prompt the operator gives you**.
  11→If a session needs a fact that is neither here nor in the docs: stop and ask; do not invent
  12→scope.
  13→
  14→## What this project is
  15→
  16→Ryde track entry for the Tencent Cloud "AI CAN DO IT" Hackathon Singapore 2026. The challenge is a
  17→**multi-agent autonomous dispute resolution system** for ride-hailing disputes: a Rider Advocate
  18→agent, a Driver Advocate agent, and a Judge agent that weighs both cases, applies company policy and
  19→issues a ruling with a confidence score.
  20→
  21→`docs/statement-extract.md` holds the challenge statement verbatim. Read it before any build work.
  22→It is the requirements floor: the locked scope below is the team's chosen subset of it, and the
  23→locked scope never widens past the statement.
  24→
  25→## Hard requirements (non-negotiable)
  26→
  27→- The project must be **original** and built on **at least one of CodeBuddy or WorkBuddy**.
  28→- **Proof of product usage is mandatory.** Without it the project is **not scored at all**. Evidence
  29→  is screenshots of CodeBuddy/WorkBuddy chat logs, minimum three, accumulated as work happens. It
  30→  cannot be reconstructed later, so capture as you go.
  31→- The project must be **demoable end to end for at least two dispute categories**.
  32→- **Inter-agent communication must be observable** to a judge: a visible log or UI showing how the
  33→  agents exchange information and build their cases.
  34→- Deliverables include a public GitHub repo with complete source, an architecture diagram, and a live
  35→  demo walkthrough.
  36→- The repository is **PUBLIC**. Never commit credentials, API keys, tokens or personal data.
  37→
  38→## Locked build scope
  39→
  40→These decisions are ruled by the team and are **not open to re-litigation**:
  41→
  42→- **Categories:** route deviation + no-show charge, end to end. No third category.
  43→- **Agents:** exactly three decide each dispute — Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge. The
  44→  Judge always emits a confidence score (0–1). Below a configurable threshold it does not rule;
  45→  the parties see only a neutral "your case is still under review" message. Escalation is MVP, not stretch.
  46→  *(Amended 2026-10-01.)* A fourth role, the **Policy & Precedent agent**, is a stretch item
  47→  built only if time allows: it reads human decisions and **proposes** policy changes, a human
  48→  approves or rejects each proposal, and it **never rules on a live case** and never edits the
  49→  policy or the code gates itself.
  50→- **Parties are spectators:** disputes arrive through a standardized intake form (category
  51→  dropdown; "other" routes to a human-review queue with a neutral message). The advocates screen
  52→  the submitted answers and may ask the party targeted follow-ups only when data conflicts or
  53→  is insufficient. No fourth intake agent. Parties never chat with the agents.
  54→- **Deterministic evidence layer:** all quantitative evidence (route deviation km/%, duration vs
  55→  estimate, fare recomputation, cancellation timestamps, chat-log signals, behaviour profile)
  56→  is computed in Python into a typed **Evidence Pack**. Agents may cite pack fields; they must
  57→  never do the arithmetic themselves.
  58→- **Policy as a swappable document:** `docs/policy.md`, rules with IDs and provenance stated
  59→  in the file. The Judge and advocates cite rule IDs. Policy text can be loaded from another
  60→  path, but it and the separately implemented Python safeguards must remain aligned; a text
  61→  replacement does not change the gates or their configured thresholds.
  62→- **Dataset as a swappable document:** synthesised corpus in `data/`, labelled with
  63→  ground-truth rulings (the correct ruling per case, by design) so replayed-run consistency is
  64→  measurable. Same swap rule.
  65→- **Observability surface (required by the statement):** a case-file view — each side's claim,
  66→  evidence and policy citations, with agent-to-agent traffic as a compact timestamped event
  67→  strip (full text one click deeper). This screen is the demo's home.
  68→- **Stack:** Python backend + plain HTML/JS front end. No heavy framework. The backend calls
  69→  Tencent Cloud's LLM API directly (key in `.env`, never committed). CodeBuddy writes the code;
  70→  it is never the runtime.
  71→- **Repo layout:** `app/` (Python backend), `ui/` (front end), `docs/` (architecture diagram,
  72→  policy set, dataset description), `evidence/` (development-process screenshots), `tools/` +
  73→  `tests/` (marked **non-app**: helper scripts and tests only; `app/` and `ui/` never import
  74→  from them). **The repo is PUBLIC at submission — never commit credentials or personal data.**
  75→- **Deployment:** local run for the live demo (real backend, real LLM calls). *(Amended
  76→  2026-10-01.)* The public link is a static replay on EdgeOne Pages of the **full loop** (filing →
  77→  the Judge withholds → a human decides → the party's status page), labelled honestly as a
  78→  replay of a real run with its date; it ships first. Optional polish on top: a hosted live
  79→  system behind one shared judge password (every page and API), a daily case cap and a daily
  80→  health check, with keys rotated before it goes up.
  81→
  82→## Non-negotiable engineering rules
  83→
  84→- Never commit `.env`, API keys, tokens, or any credential. The repo is public.
  85→- Do not read or write anything outside this folder — **this is a rule you must honour, not
  86→  something the fence guarantees.** The permission fence in `.codebuddy/settings.json` denies
  87→  reads of the planning repository path and of secret files (`.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`,
  88→  `secrets/`), denies `curl`, `wget`, `rm -rf` and `git push`, and asks before `git remote`.
  89→  It does NOT block other writes or other reads. Staying inside this folder is your job.
  90→- Verify work by running it, not by describing it. A feature is done when it has been exercised and
  91→  the real output checked.
  92→- Keep the demo path working at all times. A half-built stretch goal that breaks the main flow is
  93→  worse than no stretch goal.
  94→- **Only the CodeBuddy build lane writes `app/` and `ui/`.** Any other AI assistant used for
  95→  rescue or unblocking (e.g. another coding agent) is confined to `tools/` and `tests/` and must never
  96→  touch application code — the project's "built on CodeBuddy" claim must stay honest.
  97→  *(Amended 2026-10-01.)* A defect that lives only in `app/` or `ui/` follows the normal path:
  98→  the planning agent writes a failing test and a brief, the CodeBuddy build lane fixes it (on
  99→  the default flash model), the planning agent verifies. **One exception:** within 48 hours of
 100→  the submission deadline, if the build lane cannot land a fix in time, the rescue lane may fix
 101→  it, and every such change is logged with its reason in the commit message and in
 102→  `docs/tool-experiences.md`.
 103→
 104→## How work is done here
 105→
 106→- **One capability at a time**, verified before moving on.
 107→- Commit with a clear message after each verified step.
 108→- Log decisions as they are made. A future session starts from these files, not from memory.
 109→- **Effort follows the Demo Day rubric:** 40 of 100 points are story, design and presentation,
 110→  so `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and the demo walkthrough are deliverables on the same
 111→  footing as code — polished after the MVP floor is standing, never skipped.
 112→- **Run from this folder.** `cd ~/hermes-workspace/projects/ryde-build && codebuddy`. Sessions are
 113→  scoped by launch directory, and this folder carries its own memory file and permission fence.
 114→- **Default model is `deepseek-v4.1-flash`** (global default, x0.00 cost multiplier). Override per
 115→  task with `--model <id>` only when the work warrants the expense: GPT-5.6-Luna x0.14 is the cheap
 116→  upgrade, Kimi-K3 x1.62 for hard reasoning. Never use Primary, Deep, Sol or GPT-6-Astra here.
 117→- **Headless capture:** `codebuddy -p "<prompt>" --output-format json` returns machine-readable
 118→  results and writes a transcript to `~/.codebuddy/projects/`. Useful when the build needs to be
 119→  driven from outside the interactive session.
 120→
 121→## Layout
 122→
 123→```
 124→ryde-build/
 125→├── CODEBUDDY.md            # this file — project memory + locked scope
 126→├── README.md               # judge's entry point (judge-first: what it is → see it run → diagram)
 127→├── .codebuddy/
 128→│   └── settings.json       # permission fence
 129→├── app/                    # Python backend — agents, evidence layer, LLM calls, server, eval
 130→├── ui/                     # plain HTML/JS front end — operator console (case-file view)
 131→│   └── party/              # rider and driver intake forms, driver account, status page
 132→├── data/packs/             # two swappable dataset packs, ground-truth labelled:
 133→│                           #   organiser-style-v1 (default) and ryde-synth-v1
 134→├── docs/
 135→│   ├── statement-extract.md  # challenge statement, verbatim — the only requirements source
 136→│   ├── policy.md             # policy rule set (swappable; provenance stated in-file)
 137→│   ├── dataset.md            # dataset description + provenance
 138→│   ├── architecture.md       # required deliverable: diagram + system description
 139→│   ├── prompts.md            # how the prompts drive each agent
 140→│   ├── replay.md             # static replay export for the public link
 141→│   ├── evidence-plan.md      # §8 evidence rules and naming
 142→│   ├── tool-experiences.md   # running log of how the tools behaved
 143→│   └── build-briefs/         # one brief per build session, kept as a process record
 144→├── evidence/               # §8 screenshots (YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<topic>.png|.jpg)
 145→├── tools/                  # NON-APP helper scripts — app/ never imports from here
 146→│   └── replay/             # static replay page and its shim
 147→└── tests/                  # NON-APP tests (stdlib only)
 148→```
 149→
 150→New session briefs go in `docs/build-briefs/`. Do not create a document as a side effect of
 151→other work; each one is authored in the session whose brief names it.
